title: Business Central 29: The New IsDirty() Flag — Finally a Smarter Way to Detect Record Changes
summary: Business Central 29 introduces the IsDirty() method, a built-in flag that detects whether a record has been modified since retrieval. This simplifies validation logic, sync operations, and audit trails by eliminating the need for manual field comparisons or temporary records.
key_points: IsDirty() returns true if a record has changed since being loaded or written, false if untouched
Replaces error-prone patterns like temporary record copies or manual field tracking
Works alongside IsEmpty() and IsTemporary() to provide three essential record state checks
Reduces unnecessary Modify() calls in high-volume or integration scenarios
Makes code cleaner and easier to maintain by eliminating boilerplate dirty-flag logic

quotes.text: The new IsDirty() method lets you check whether a record has been modified since it was retrieved or last written.
quotes.why_it_matters: This is the core capability - it provides a built-in way to detect changes without manual workarounds or hacks.

quotes.text: IsDirty() now joins two other small-but-essential record flags that AL developers rely on: IsEmpty() and IsTemporary().
quotes.why_it_matters: It completes a trio of record state checks that developers use constantly when working with records.

quotes.text: It's the kind of quality-of-life upgrade that makes Business Central feel more modern, more predictable, and more fun to build on.
quotes.why_it_matters: Highlights the practical developer experience improvement from having this built-in capability rather than custom solutions.
